svg.aria-label: Two documentation caps locked together: the heaviest generated page has 39,245 bytes of room and is growing 6,535 a day, which is six days; its only remedy needs 13,105 bytes in a table of contents that has 7,611 left.
svg.text: Measured on `main` at 15f4790, 7 November 2026. Every figure is counted in this container.
THE CAP THAT IS ABOUT TO FIRE
The heaviest generated page — /docs/api-reference/signals — against 90% of its cap
Growing 6,535 bytes a day — 466,077 on 1 Nov to 498,752 on 6 Nov, read off the committed reference.
39,245 ÷ 6,535 = six days. About 13 November, on whichever lane's branch is running.
ITS ONLY REMEDY, WHICH THE CAP HAS PRE-AGREED SINCE THE DAY IT SHIPPED
Cut the page along its 60 modules — one address each. Priced for the first time today:
THE FILE THAT WOULD HAVE TO PAY FOR IT
The table of contents — the one file in the search index a reader sits in front of and waits for
The cut asks for 13,105. It overruns the file by 5,494 bytes — and cutting every door asks 73,627.
Raising the cap is refused by the cap's own argument. Cutting the page does not fit. The third way is
one word on #778 — 0353 takes the prose bill from 79,080 to 35,928 and gives the contents file room to shard.
